headline: Karnataka voter roll audit finds over 17,000 parent-child age errors
summary: More than 17,000 entries in Karnataka's revised electoral rolls list parents younger than, the same age as, or under 15 years older than their children, The Hindu reported. After October's revision deleted 99.3 lakh names, slashing rolls 17.9%, state election officials agreed to verify sample errors.
why_it_matters: Flawed voter-roll purges risk disenfranchising genuine citizens while triggering severe real-world consequences, as some BJP-ruled states cite deletions to deny ration cards and passport renewals.

headline: England flu hospital admissions jump nearly 80% amid low vaccine uptake
summary: Flu hospitalisations in England jumped nearly 80% in a week to pre-Covid highs, the UK Health Security Agency said. Just 34% of almost 9.5 million eligible high-risk under-65s received jabs by 22 November. Some hospitals have reintroduced masks as officials expect indoor Christmas socialising to accelerate spread.
why_it_matters: An early, mutated H1N1 flu wave could overwhelm stretched NHS wards already reliant on corridor care, increasing winter disruption and mortality among unvaccinated vulnerable groups.
source_search: England flu hospital admissions jump nearly 80% amid low vaccine uptake BBC

headline: Reform UK pledges free English hospital parking funded by foreign patient fees
summary: Reform UK pledged to abolish NHS hospital parking fees in England for patients, visitors and staff if elected. The party would cover the £285m annual cost by raising overseas visitor charges to 200% of national tariffs, billing emergency and GP visits, and requiring non-reciprocal visitors' insurance.
why_it_matters: Health analysts question whether higher foreign-visitor surcharges can realistically replace £300m in trust parking revenue without raising NHS administrative costs and worsening space shortages.
source_search: Reform UK pledges free English hospital parking funded by foreign patient fees BBC

headline: Cricket Australia widens sandpapergate inquiry to include 2017–18 Ashes
summary: Cricket Australia expanded its independent sandpapergate inquiry to examine ball-management practices during the 2017–18 Ashes and the 2018 South Africa tour. Reignited by Usman Khawaja's autobiography, the six-week voluntary forum offers confidentiality without retrospective sanctions. Officials pledged to release the full report within 30 days of receiving it.
why_it_matters: Reopening questions over earlier ball-tampering puts renewed scrutiny on current Test captain Pat Cummins and frontline bowlers who have long denied prior knowledge.
source_search: Cricket Australia widens sandpapergate inquiry to include 2017–18 Ashes BBC Sport

headline: Oscar-winning 'Schindler's List' and 'Jurassic Park' producer Gerald Molen dies at 91
summary: Gerald R. Molen, the Oscar-winning producer of Steven Spielberg's 1994 best picture 'Schindler's List,' died at 91, his great-niece announced Sunday. Beginning as a studio driver, Molen partnered with Spielberg in 1985, producing 'Jurassic Park,' 'Minority Report,' 'Hook' and 'Rain Man,' alongside Amblin hits like 'Twister.'
why_it_matters: Molen's death marks the passing of a veteran studio executive who helped shape modern Hollywood blockbusters and prestige cinema during Amblin Entertainment's peak era.

headline: Welsh health chief drops English NHS job after damning leadership review
summary: Betsi Cadwaladr Health Board chief Carol Shillabeer withdrew from leading England's Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Trust following a damning review. Published Tuesday, the independent inquiry found senior management prioritised finances and targets over patient care quality. Shillabeer will depart her Welsh post on 3 January 2027.
why_it_matters: Leadership accountability across UK health systems faces intense scrutiny after special measures failed to fix management culture at Wales's largest health board.
source_search: Welsh health chief drops English NHS job after damning leadership review BBC
